This endows the G2-based electrolyte high ionic conductivity, but regretfully, impedes $Na^{+}$ desolvation. DOL is a low polarity and low melting point ( $-95\ ^{\circ}C$ ) cyclic ether that exhibits dipole-dipole interactions with G2. Explicitly, ${}^{1}H$ and ${}^{17}O$ nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) were studied in Figure 2b; Figure S1 (Supporting Information). ${}^{1}H$ (G2) displays an upfield chemical shift in G2/DOL than G2, while the chemical shift of the ${}^{17}O$ (G2) shifts downfield. This implies that the dipole-dipole interactions between G2 and DOL weaken the shielding effect of electron clouds of O (G2) on atomic nucleus, indicating a decrease in the electron cloud density of O (G2). This demonstrates that DOL attenuates the electronegativity of donor O (G2), thereby diminishing the coordination of G2. $^{[16]}$ Consequently, DOL was blended into 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2 with a volume ratio of 3:1 to prepare 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2/DOL for the low-temperature adaptive electrolyte. 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2 as the reference electrolyte was compared and analyzed.

The baseline electrolyte was prepared by dissolving $NaPF_{6}$ in a mixture of EC: EMC = 3:7 to form a concentration of 0.8 mol $L^{-1}$ . Then, 1% (Mass ratio) NaDFP, TDFP, TMSP was added into the baseline electrolyte to prepare corresponding electrolyte. All electrolytes were prepared in a dry argon filled glove box with both moisture and oxygen concentrations below 0.1 ppm. NFM was purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co, Ltd., HC was purchased from Kuraray Co Ltd. The pouch test cells with NFM cathode (120 mAh $g^{-1}$ at 0.1C), HC anode (290 mAh $g^{-1}$ at 0.05C), and Celgard 2700 separator were assembled using the conventional assembly method. Thereinto, NFM active material, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotube (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and Maleic acid were dispersed in N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) with a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate to prepare the NFM cathode.

evidence_ledger.quote: In summary, we have systematically studied carbonate-based electrolytes for NFM/HC SIBs, showing that PC-based electrolytes outperform in terms of capacity retention and safety, as compared with the EC-based electrolytes. Combined with multiple additives, the PC/EMC electrolyte further promotes the formation of a protective interfacial layer, which consequently mitigates parasitic reactions between the electrodes and electrolyte and suppresses chemical dissolution of transition metal ions from the desodiated (charged) NFM. Finally, we demonstrated that a 0.8 M NaPF $_{6}$ /PC-EMC optimized by the second-generation additives not only enables the NFM/HC pouch cell to reversibly cycle over 2500 cycles but also makes the cell safer.

evidence_ledger.paper_id: 0030_Li 等 - 2025 - An electrolyte design strategy for commercial all-climate pouch sodium-ion batteries
evidence_ledger.quote: A type of wide temperature range electrolyte design strategy incorporating trifunctional trimethylsilyl methanesulfonate (TMSS) additive in specific carbonate ester is developed to enhance the all-climate performance of commercial pouch $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). The incorporation of TMSS serves optimizing the solvation structure to accelerate the reaction kinetics, eliminating residual $H_{2}O/HF$ from the electrolyte, and promoting the formation of high-quality interface films. The capacity retention of the pouch NFM/HC cells with TMSS is effectively enhanced at high-voltage of 4.0 V and wide-temperature range from $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . The cell delivers a high capacity retention of 80 % after 700 cycles at $25\ ^{\circ}C$ , while the initial energy density is as high as 117 Wh kg $^{-1}$ and maintains 103 Wh kg $^{-1}$ after 300 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ and 1C (1C = 900 mA), achieving an 18.2 % increase in energy density. In addition, no obvious gas evolution can be observed when pouch cell is stored at $60\ ^{\circ}C$ and the low-temperature discharge at $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ achieves a 14.76 % increase in capacity at 0.5C. This work demonstrates the feasibility of TMSS in SIBs, and also put insight on the rational electrolyte design of SIBs.

2.4. Electrochemical Performance of Full Cell
We also have tested the low-temperature performance of 0.5 M NaPF $_{6}$ G2/DOL in the cathode material of SIBs. Na $_{3}$ V $_{2}$ (PO $_{4}$ ) $_{3}$ was selected as the cathode with Na metal anode to assemble a coin cell. Rate performance of Na||NVP coupled with both electrolytes were evaluated. NVP paired with 0.5 M NaPF $_{6}$ G2/DOL achieves a capacity of up to 74.7 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 10 C, while it exclusively remains 60.6 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 10 C with 0.5 M NaPF $_{6}$ G2, as demonstrated in Figures S22–S24 (Supporting Information). Basic physical and thermochemical properties of the electrolytes were first investigated by using $NaPF_{6}$ as the solute and mixed carbonate as the solvent. Typically, cyclic PC and EC are of high dielectric constant and high viscosity, while linear EMC, DMC and DEC feature are of much lower viscosity and relatively lower dielectric constant (Table S1) [37]. 2.1 Electrolyte and pouch cell preparation
Battery grade solvents of propylene carbonate (PC), ethylene carbonate (EC), ethyl methyl carbonate (EMC), dimethyl carbonate (DMC), diethyl carbonate (DEC) and fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC) were obtained from Shenzhen CAPCHEM Technology Co., Ltd, China, and used as received. Sodium hexafluorophosphate $(\mathrm{NaPF}_6$ , KISHIDA Chemical Co., Ltd, Japan) was dissolved into cold solvent mixtures with different volume ratios. Water contents of all resultant electrolytes were determined by the Karl Fischer titration to be lower than $15~\mathrm{ppm}$ .

The $NaNi_{1/3}Fe_{1/3}Mn_{1/3}O_{2}$ (NFM) cathode material was scale-up synthesized as described previously [17]. The NFM cathode and hard carbon (HC) anode were prepared by coating slurries consisting of 92 wt.% active material, 4 wt.% super P, and 4 wt.% polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) in N-Methyl-2-pyrrolidone (NMP) onto an aluminum foil, respectively. The cathode-separator-anode assembles were stacked and packaged into a plastic-laminated aluminum pouch. After heating at 80 °C for 48 h under vacuum, the dried pouch cells were moved into a glove box for injecting electrolyte.

Before testing, the pouch cells were subject to a series of pre-processes, consisting of overnight aging and formation at room temperature by charging from open circuit voltage (OCV) to 4.0 V at 0.02 C, followed by aging at 45 °C for 24 h, degassing, and vacuum sealing. The electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) of pouch cells at 100% SOC was measured by Solartron with an amplitude of 5 mV in 0.01-105 Hz frequency range. The battery internal resistance (AC) was measured by an IT5100 battery tester.

citations.quote: In summary, we have systematically studied carbonate-based electrolytes for NFM/HC SIBs, showing that PC-based electrolytes outperform in terms of capacity retention and safety, as compared with the EC-based electrolytes. Combined with multiple additives, the PC/EMC electrolyte further promotes the formation of a protective interfacial layer, which consequently mitigates parasitic reactions between the electrodes and electrolyte and suppresses chemical dissolution of transition metal ions from the desodiated (charged) NFM. Finally, we demonstrated that a 0.8 M NaPF $_{6}$ /PC-EMC optimized by the second-generation additives not only enables the NFM/HC pouch cell to reversibly cycle over 2500 cycles but also makes the cell safer.

citations.chunk_id: 0030_Li 等 - 2025 - An electrolyte design strategy for commercial all-climate pouch sodium-ion batteries::sec2::child0
citations.quote: A type of wide temperature range electrolyte design strategy incorporating trifunctional trimethylsilyl methanesulfonate (TMSS) additive in specific carbonate ester is developed to enhance the all-climate performance of commercial pouch $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). The incorporation of TMSS serves optimizing the solvation structure to accelerate the reaction kinetics, eliminating residual $H_{2}O/HF$ from the electrolyte, and promoting the formation of high-quality interface films. The capacity retention of the pouch NFM/HC cells with TMSS is effectively enhanced at high-voltage of 4.0 V and wide-temperature range from $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . The cell delivers a high capacity retention of 80 % after 700 cycles at $25\ ^{\circ}C$ , while the initial energy density is as high as 117 Wh kg $^{-1}$ and maintains 103 Wh kg $^{-1}$ after 300 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ and 1C (1C = 900 mA), achieving an 18.2 % increase in energy density. In addition, no obvious gas evolution can be observed when pouch cell is stored at $60\ ^{\circ}C$ and the low-temperature discharge at $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ achieves a 14.76 % increase in capacity at 0.5C. This work demonstrates the feasibility of TMSS in SIBs, and also put insight on the rational electrolyte design of SIBs.

citations.quote: To begin with, in order to pre-evaluate the practicability of ether and carbonate ester as the electrolyte in pouch cells, comparative tests were first carried out, as shown in Fig. S1. Although the ether electrolytes have a high initial capacity, their cycling stability is poor, with a capacity retention rate of only 77.38 after 105 cycles, while the carbonate electrolytes have a capacity retention rate of 87.49 %. The gas production behaviour of ether and carbonate ester during long-term cycling at a cut-off voltage of 4.0 V at 45°C was monitored using differential electrochemical mass spectrometry (Fig. S2). It was observed that ether produced a greater quantity of gases, including methane and carbon monoxide, in comparison to carbonate ester. This may be a contributing factor to the unsuitability of ether for use in pouch cells, due to the rapid consumption of electrolyte, which results in a rapid decline in battery capacity. The electrolyte formula employs a combination of 1 mol/L NaPF $_{6}$ , cyclic ester EC and linear ester EMC in a mass ratio of 3:7 (called Baseline electrolyte), augmented by the incorporation of 3 wt% TMSS as a functional additive. The introduction of linear esters engenders a reduction in viscosity and an enhanced capacity to dissolve sodium salts in the electrolyte as a whole, thereby facilitating an improvement in the fluidity and ion conductivity of the electrolyte.

citations.chunk_id: 0009_Cui 等 - 2025 - A Temperature-Adapted Ultraweakly Solvating Electrolyte for Cold-Resistant Sodium-Ion Batteries::sec2::child0
citations.quote: Primarily, $Na^{+}-O$ (DOL) has a lower binding energy compared to $Na^{+}-O$ (G2), as shown in Figure 2a. Additionally, $Na^{+}$ can form a stable five-membered chelation structure with the negative-charged multidentate oxygen of G2 molecules. This endows the G2-based electrolyte high ionic conductivity, but regretfully, impedes $Na^{+}$ desolvation. DOL is a low polarity and low melting point ( $-95\ ^{\circ}C$ ) cyclic ether that exhibits dipole-dipole interactions with G2. Explicitly, ${}^{1}H$ and ${}^{17}O$ nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) were studied in Figure 2b; Figure S1 (Supporting Information). ${}^{1}H$ (G2) displays an upfield chemical shift in G2/DOL than G2, while the chemical shift of the ${}^{17}O$ (G2) shifts downfield. This implies that the dipole-dipole interactions between G2 and DOL weaken the shielding effect of electron clouds of O (G2) on atomic nucleus, indicating a decrease in the electron cloud density of O (G2). This demonstrates that DOL attenuates the electronegativity of donor O (G2), thereby diminishing the coordination of G2. $^{[16]}$ Consequently, DOL was blended into 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2 with a volume ratio of 3:1 to prepare 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2/DOL for the low-temperature adaptive electrolyte. 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2 as the reference electrolyte was compared and analyzed.

Sodium-ion batteries are applied to cold-resistant energy storage hindered by phase transitions and sluggish $Na^{+}$ migration of traditional carbonate-based electrolytes at low temperatures. 2.4. Electrochemical Performance of Full Cell
We also have tested the low-temperature performance of 0.5 M NaPF $_{6}$ G2/DOL in the cathode material of SIBs. Na $_{3}$ V $_{2}$ (PO $_{4}$ ) $_{3}$ was selected as the cathode with Na metal anode to assemble a coin cell. Rate performance of Na||NVP coupled with both electrolytes were evaluated. NVP paired with 0.5 M NaPF $_{6}$ G2/DOL achieves a capacity of up to 74.7 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 10 C, while it exclusively remains 60.6 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 10 C with 0.5 M NaPF $_{6}$ G2, as demonstrated in Figures S22–S24 (Supporting Information). Surprisingly, it can operate normally at LT, and specifically preserve a capacity of 79.8 mAh g $^{-1}$ at $-40$ °C, which is equivalent to 80.0% of the capacity at 25 °C in Figure S25 (Supporting Information). citations.chunk_id: 0017_Fan 等 - 2026 - Difluorophosphate-based electrolyte for pouch sodium-ion batteries with a wide temperature range::sec4::child0
citations.quote: The main raw materials used for preparing functional electrolytes, including ethylene carbonate (EC), ethyl methyl carbonate (EMC), sodium hexafluorophosphate $\left(\mathrm{NaPF}_{6}\right)$ , NaDFP, TMSP and TDFP were provided by the Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. The baseline electrolyte was prepared by dissolving $NaPF_{6}$ in a mixture of EC: EMC = 3:7 to form a concentration of 0.8 mol $L^{-1}$ . Then, 1% (Mass ratio) NaDFP, TDFP, TMSP was added into the baseline electrolyte to prepare corresponding electrolyte. All electrolytes were prepared in a dry argon filled glove box with both moisture and oxygen concentrations below 0.1 ppm. NFM was purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co, Ltd., HC was purchased from Kuraray Co Ltd. The pouch test cells with NFM cathode (120 mAh $g^{-1}$ at 0.1C), HC anode (290 mAh $g^{-1}$ at 0.05C), and Celgard 2700 separator were assembled using the conventional assembly method. Thereinto, NFM active material, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotube (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and Maleic acid were dispersed in N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) with a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate to prepare the NFM cathode.

citations.chunk_id: 0017_Fan 等 - 2026 - Difluorophosphate-based electrolyte for pouch sodium-ion batteries with a wide temperature range::sec4::child0
citations.quote: The main raw materials used for preparing functional electrolytes, including ethylene carbonate (EC), ethyl methyl carbonate (EMC), sodium hexafluorophosphate $\left(\mathrm{NaPF}_{6}\right)$ , NaDFP, TMSP and TDFP were provided by the Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. The baseline electrolyte was prepared by dissolving $NaPF_{6}$ in a mixture of EC: EMC = 3:7 to form a concentration of 0.8 mol $L^{-1}$ . Then, 1% (Mass ratio) NaDFP, TDFP, TMSP was added into the baseline electrolyte to prepare corresponding electrolyte. All electrolytes were prepared in a dry argon filled glove box with both moisture and oxygen concentrations below 0.1 ppm. NFM was purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co, Ltd., HC was purchased from Kuraray Co Ltd. The pouch test cells with NFM cathode (120 mAh $g^{-1}$ at 0.1C), HC anode (290 mAh $g^{-1}$ at 0.05C), and Celgard 2700 separator were assembled using the conventional assembly method. Thereinto, NFM active material, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotube (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and Maleic acid were dispersed in N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) with a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate to prepare the NFM cathode.

citations.quote:
The RDFs exhibit a maximum at $2.35\AA$ for $\mathrm{Na^{+} - O}$ interactions, indicating that the sodium ion is surrounded by DG molecules as the first solvated sheath. The calculated coordination number (CN) of Na-O in 0.5M-D (2.18) is higher than that in 1M-D (1.99), and it further increases to

2.26 at $-30^{\circ}C$ , which supports the conclusion that more DG enters the solvated sheath. $^{[13]}$

To gain insight into the practicality of 0.5M-D in subzero environments, LMNM'T//Na half cells were assembled to estimate the electrochemical performance, and the common electrolyte 1M NaPF $_{6}$ in propylene carbonate with 5 vol. % fluoroethylene carbonate (denoted as PC) was chosen as a comparison. The LMNM'T cathode materials were prepared by simple solid-state reaction (as described in the experimental section at Supporting Information) and the phase was verified by X-ray diffraction (XRD) (Figure S2). Figure 2a–b manifests the charge/discharge voltage curves with different electrolytes at a specific current of 0.1C (1C = 173 mA g $^{-1}$ ). When tested at 25°C, both batteries with PC and 0.5M-D provide high discharge capacity (93.6 and 98.7 mAh g $^{-1}$ ) with a complete solid solution reaction. But at a sub-zero temperature of $-20$ °C, the cells with PC electrolyte deliver significant polarization which further boosts at $-30$ °C.

3. Results and discussion
Basic physical and thermochemical properties of the electrolytes were first investigated by using $NaPF_{6}$ as the solute and mixed carbonate as the solvent. Typically, cyclic PC and EC are of high dielectric constant and high viscosity, while linear EMC, DMC and DEC feature are of much lower viscosity and relatively lower dielectric constant (Table S1) [37]. The $NaPF_{6}$ was used as the solute because it has similar electrochemical properties as $LiPF_{6}$ and much better thermal stability. $NaPF_{6}$ is stable up to $\sim400\ ^{\circ}C$ , as indicated by the TG and DSC curves in Fig.1a. The little peak at about $300\ ^{\circ}C$ is the melting endothermic peak of $NaPF_{6}$ as the literature reported. [38]

2.1 Electrolyte and pouch cell preparation
Battery grade solvents of propylene carbonate (PC), ethylene carbonate (EC), ethyl methyl carbonate (EMC), dimethyl carbonate (DMC), diethyl carbonate (DEC) and fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC) were obtained from Shenzhen CAPCHEM Technology Co., Ltd, China, and used as received. Sodium hexafluorophosphate $(\mathrm{NaPF}_6$ , KISHIDA Chemical Co., Ltd, Japan) was dissolved into cold solvent mixtures with different volume ratios. Water contents of all resultant electrolytes were determined by the Karl Fischer titration to be lower than $15~\mathrm{ppm}$ .

The $NaNi_{1/3}Fe_{1/3}Mn_{1/3}O_{2}$ (NFM) cathode material was scale-up synthesized as described previously [17]. The NFM cathode and hard carbon (HC) anode were prepared by coating slurries consisting of 92 wt.% active material, 4 wt.% super P, and 4 wt.% polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) in N-Methyl-2-pyrrolidone (NMP) onto an aluminum foil, respectively. The cathode-separator-anode assembles were stacked and packaged into a plastic-laminated aluminum pouch. After heating at 80 °C for 48 h under vacuum, the dried pouch cells were moved into a glove box for injecting electrolyte.

In the binary PC/EMC (1:1, v/v) system, the highest conductivity of 7.45 mS cm $^{-1}$ at 20 °C is observed at 0.8 M NaPF $_{6}$ (Fig. 1b). Before testing, the pouch cells were subject to a series of pre-processes, consisting of overnight aging and formation at room temperature by charging from open circuit voltage (OCV) to 4.0 V at 0.02 C, followed by aging at 45 °C for 24 h, degassing, and vacuum sealing. The battery internal resistance (AC) was measured by an IT5100 battery tester.

The cycling performance of cells was tested at 1 C, and the rate characteristic of pouch cells was conducted at 0.2 C, 0.5 C, 1 C, 2 C, 3 C, 5 C, and 0.2 C, respectively. Before testing, the pouch cells were subject to a series of pre-processes, consisting of overnight aging and formation at room temperature by charging from open circuit voltage (OCV) to 4.0 V at 0.02 C, followed by aging at 45 °C for 24 h, degassing, and vacuum sealing. The electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) of pouch cells at 100% SOC was measured by Solartron with an amplitude of 5 mV in 0.01-105 Hz frequency range. The battery internal resistance (AC) was measured by an IT5100 battery tester.

association_citations.quote: Therefore, in the present work, the PC/EMC solvent system was preferably selected to investigate the effect of solvent ratio and salt concentration. In the binary PC/EMC (1:1, v/v) system, the highest conductivity of 7.45 mS cm $^{-1}$ at 20 °C is observed at 0.8 M NaPF $_{6}$ (Fig. 1b). It is also found that the conductivity of electrolyte changes with the solvent ratio changing. The viscosity of 0.8 M NaPF $_{6}$ electrolyte is gradually increased with the PC content rising. With an increase in the PC content, the conductivity increases markedly in the range lower than 40%, reaches a maximum at 60% (i.e., PC/EMC=3/2), and inversely declines in the range higher than 60% (Fig. 1c). On the other hand, the electrolytes with PC content lower than 40% are much easier to wet the nonpolar polypropylene-polyethylene separator. Complete wetting of the separator typically takes no more than 10 seconds, as indicated by the wetting angles and wettability in Fig. S1 and Fig. S2. Based on the above results, five 0.8 M NaPF $_{6}$ electrolytes were prepared by using 2 wt% FEC additive and PC/EMC, PC/DMC, EC/EMC, EC/DMC and EC/DEC mixed solvents (all having a 2:3 cyclic/linear carbonate ratio), respectively. It is shown that the ionic conductivity of these electrolytes is increased in the order of EC/DMC > PC/DMC > EC/EMC > PC/EMC > EC/DEC, whereas the viscosity is changed nearly in an opposite order of EC/DEC > EC/EMC > PC/EMC > PC/DMC ≈ EC/DMC (Fig. 2a).

Basic physical and thermochemical properties of the electrolytes were first investigated by using $NaPF_{6}$ as the solute and mixed carbonate as the solvent. 2.1 Electrolyte and pouch cell preparation
Battery grade solvents of propylene carbonate (PC), ethylene carbonate (EC), ethyl methyl carbonate (EMC), dimethyl carbonate (DMC), diethyl carbonate (DEC) and fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC) were obtained from Shenzhen CAPCHEM Technology Co., Ltd, China, and used as received. Sodium hexafluorophosphate $(\mathrm{NaPF}_6$ , KISHIDA Chemical Co., Ltd, Japan) was dissolved into cold solvent mixtures with different volume ratios. Water contents of all resultant electrolytes were determined by the Karl Fischer titration to be lower than $15~\mathrm{ppm}$ .

The $NaNi_{1/3}Fe_{1/3}Mn_{1/3}O_{2}$ (NFM) cathode material was scale-up synthesized as described previously [17]. The NFM cathode and hard carbon (HC) anode were prepared by coating slurries consisting of 92 wt.% active material, 4 wt.% super P, and 4 wt.% polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) in N-Methyl-2-pyrrolidone (NMP) onto an aluminum foil, respectively. The cathode-separator-anode assembles were stacked and packaged into a plastic-laminated aluminum pouch. After heating at 80 °C for 48 h under vacuum, the dried pouch cells were moved into a glove box for injecting electrolyte.

citations.quote: In summary, we have systematically studied carbonate-based electrolytes for NFM/HC SIBs, showing that PC-based electrolytes outperform in terms of capacity retention and safety, as compared with the EC-based electrolytes. Combined with multiple additives, the PC/EMC electrolyte further promotes the formation of a protective interfacial layer, which consequently mitigates parasitic reactions between the electrodes and electrolyte and suppresses chemical dissolution of transition metal ions from the desodiated (charged) NFM. Finally, we demonstrated that a 0.8 M NaPF $_{6}$ /PC-EMC optimized by the second-generation additives not only enables the NFM/HC pouch cell to reversibly cycle over 2500 cycles but also makes the cell safer.

unaddressed_requirements: Exact composition of the 'second-generation additive' package reported for the optimized 0.8 M NaPF6/PC-EMC electrolyte, which the candidate does not reproduce (candidate has only 2 wt% FEC).
review.experimental_association: The candidate formulation matches the experimentally tested set: 0.8 M NaPF6 in PC/EMC (2:3 cyclic/linear) with 2 wt% FEC, evaluated in NFM/HC pouch cells cycled at 1.5-3.8 V, with low-temperature capacity retention measured relative to room temperature; the -30 °C retention value therefore transfers directly to this candidate's composition and cell format, with the caveat that the paper's final 'second-generation additive' optimized electrolyte is not fully specified.

citations.chunk_id: 0030_Li 等 - 2025 - An electrolyte design strategy for commercial all-climate pouch sodium-ion batteries::sec2::child0
citations.quote: A type of wide temperature range electrolyte design strategy incorporating trifunctional trimethylsilyl methanesulfonate (TMSS) additive in specific carbonate ester is developed to enhance the all-climate performance of commercial pouch $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). The incorporation of TMSS serves optimizing the solvation structure to accelerate the reaction kinetics, eliminating residual $H_{2}O/HF$ from the electrolyte, and promoting the formation of high-quality interface films. The capacity retention of the pouch NFM/HC cells with TMSS is effectively enhanced at high-voltage of 4.0 V and wide-temperature range from $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . The cell delivers a high capacity retention of 80 % after 700 cycles at $25\ ^{\circ}C$ , while the initial energy density is as high as 117 Wh kg $^{-1}$ and maintains 103 Wh kg $^{-1}$ after 300 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ and 1C (1C = 900 mA), achieving an 18.2 % increase in energy density. In addition, no obvious gas evolution can be observed when pouch cell is stored at $60\ ^{\circ}C$ and the low-temperature discharge at $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ achieves a 14.76 % increase in capacity at 0.5C. This work demonstrates the feasibility of TMSS in SIBs, and also put insight on the rational electrolyte design of SIBs.

citations.quote: To begin with, in order to pre-evaluate the practicability of ether and carbonate ester as the electrolyte in pouch cells, comparative tests were first carried out, as shown in Fig. S1. Although the ether electrolytes have a high initial capacity, their cycling stability is poor, with a capacity retention rate of only 77.38 after 105 cycles, while the carbonate electrolytes have a capacity retention rate of 87.49 %. The gas production behaviour of ether and carbonate ester during long-term cycling at a cut-off voltage of 4.0 V at 45°C was monitored using differential electrochemical mass spectrometry (Fig. S2). It was observed that ether produced a greater quantity of gases, including methane and carbon monoxide, in comparison to carbonate ester. This may be a contributing factor to the unsuitability of ether for use in pouch cells, due to the rapid consumption of electrolyte, which results in a rapid decline in battery capacity. The electrolyte formula employs a combination of 1 mol/L NaPF $_{6}$ , cyclic ester EC and linear ester EMC in a mass ratio of 3:7 (called Baseline electrolyte), augmented by the incorporation of 3 wt% TMSS as a functional additive. The introduction of linear esters engenders a reduction in viscosity and an enhanced capacity to dissolve sodium salts in the electrolyte as a whole, thereby facilitating an improvement in the fluidity and ion conductivity of the electrolyte.

citations.chunk_id: 0030_Li 等 - 2025 - An electrolyte design strategy for commercial all-climate pouch sodium-ion batteries::sec2::child0
citations.quote: A type of wide temperature range electrolyte design strategy incorporating trifunctional trimethylsilyl methanesulfonate (TMSS) additive in specific carbonate ester is developed to enhance the all-climate performance of commercial pouch $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). The incorporation of TMSS serves optimizing the solvation structure to accelerate the reaction kinetics, eliminating residual $H_{2}O/HF$ from the electrolyte, and promoting the formation of high-quality interface films. The capacity retention of the pouch NFM/HC cells with TMSS is effectively enhanced at high-voltage of 4.0 V and wide-temperature range from $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . The cell delivers a high capacity retention of 80 % after 700 cycles at $25\ ^{\circ}C$ , while the initial energy density is as high as 117 Wh kg $^{-1}$ and maintains 103 Wh kg $^{-1}$ after 300 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ and 1C (1C = 900 mA), achieving an 18.2 % increase in energy density. In addition, no obvious gas evolution can be observed when pouch cell is stored at $60\ ^{\circ}C$ and the low-temperature discharge at $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ achieves a 14.76 % increase in capacity at 0.5C. This work demonstrates the feasibility of TMSS in SIBs, and also put insight on the rational electrolyte design of SIBs.

association_citations.quote: To begin with, in order to pre-evaluate the practicability of ether and carbonate ester as the electrolyte in pouch cells, comparative tests were first carried out, as shown in Fig. S1. Although the ether electrolytes have a high initial capacity, their cycling stability is poor, with a capacity retention rate of only 77.38 after 105 cycles, while the carbonate electrolytes have a capacity retention rate of 87.49 %. The gas production behaviour of ether and carbonate ester during long-term cycling at a cut-off voltage of 4.0 V at 45°C was monitored using differential electrochemical mass spectrometry (Fig. S2). It was observed that ether produced a greater quantity of gases, including methane and carbon monoxide, in comparison to carbonate ester. This may be a contributing factor to the unsuitability of ether for use in pouch cells, due to the rapid consumption of electrolyte, which results in a rapid decline in battery capacity. The introduction of linear esters engenders a reduction in viscosity and an enhanced capacity to dissolve sodium salts in the electrolyte as a whole, thereby facilitating an improvement in the fluidity and ion conductivity of the electrolyte.

citations.quote: Primarily, $Na^{+}-O$ (DOL) has a lower binding energy compared to $Na^{+}-O$ (G2), as shown in Figure 2a. Additionally, $Na^{+}$ can form a stable five-membered chelation structure with the negative-charged multidentate oxygen of G2 molecules. This endows the G2-based electrolyte high ionic conductivity, but regretfully, impedes $Na^{+}$ desolvation. DOL is a low polarity and low melting point ( $-95\ ^{\circ}C$ ) cyclic ether that exhibits dipole-dipole interactions with G2. Explicitly, ${}^{1}H$ and ${}^{17}O$ nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) were studied in Figure 2b; Figure S1 (Supporting Information). ${}^{1}H$ (G2) displays an upfield chemical shift in G2/DOL than G2, while the chemical shift of the ${}^{17}O$ (G2) shifts downfield. This implies that the dipole-dipole interactions between G2 and DOL weaken the shielding effect of electron clouds of O (G2) on atomic nucleus, indicating a decrease in the electron cloud density of O (G2). This demonstrates that DOL attenuates the electronegativity of donor O (G2), thereby diminishing the coordination of G2. $^{[16]}$ Consequently, DOL was blended into 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2 with a volume ratio of 3:1 to prepare 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2/DOL for the low-temperature adaptive electrolyte. 0.5 M $NaPF_{6}$ G2 as the reference electrolyte was compared and analyzed.

citations.chunk_id: 0017_Fan 等 - 2026 - Difluorophosphate-based electrolyte for pouch sodium-ion batteries with a wide temperature range::sec4::child0
citations.quote: The main raw materials used for preparing functional electrolytes, including ethylene carbonate (EC), ethyl methyl carbonate (EMC), sodium hexafluorophosphate $\left(\mathrm{NaPF}_{6}\right)$ , NaDFP, TMSP and TDFP were provided by the Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. The baseline electrolyte was prepared by dissolving $NaPF_{6}$ in a mixture of EC: EMC = 3:7 to form a concentration of 0.8 mol $L^{-1}$ . Then, 1% (Mass ratio) NaDFP, TDFP, TMSP was added into the baseline electrolyte to prepare corresponding electrolyte. All electrolytes were prepared in a dry argon filled glove box with both moisture and oxygen concentrations below 0.1 ppm. NFM was purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co, Ltd., HC was purchased from Kuraray Co Ltd. The pouch test cells with NFM cathode (120 mAh $g^{-1}$ at 0.1C), HC anode (290 mAh $g^{-1}$ at 0.05C), and Celgard 2700 separator were assembled using the conventional assembly method. Thereinto, NFM active material, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotube (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and Maleic acid were dispersed in N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) with a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate to prepare the NFM cathode.

citations.quote:
The RDFs exhibit a maximum at $2.35\AA$ for $\mathrm{Na^{+} - O}$ interactions, indicating that the sodium ion is surrounded by DG molecules as the first solvated sheath. The calculated coordination number (CN) of Na-O in 0.5M-D (2.18) is higher than that in 1M-D (1.99), and it further increases to

2.26 at $-30^{\circ}C$ , which supports the conclusion that more DG enters the solvated sheath. $^{[13]}$

To gain insight into the practicality of 0.5M-D in subzero environments, LMNM'T//Na half cells were assembled to estimate the electrochemical performance, and the common electrolyte 1M NaPF $_{6}$ in propylene carbonate with 5 vol. % fluoroethylene carbonate (denoted as PC) was chosen as a comparison. The LMNM'T cathode materials were prepared by simple solid-state reaction (as described in the experimental section at Supporting Information) and the phase was verified by X-ray diffraction (XRD) (Figure S2). Figure 2a–b manifests the charge/discharge voltage curves with different electrolytes at a specific current of 0.1C (1C = 173 mA g $^{-1}$ ). When tested at 25°C, both batteries with PC and 0.5M-D provide high discharge capacity (93.6 and 98.7 mAh g $^{-1}$ ) with a complete solid solution reaction. But at a sub-zero temperature of $-20$ °C, the cells with PC electrolyte deliver significant polarization which further boosts at $-30$ °C.

## 配方筛选结果
获得文献支持的候选：cui-0.5M-G2-DOL。

### 候选资料：cui-0.5M-G2-DOL（通过筛选）

盐：NaPF6；浓度：0.5 mol L⁻¹；NaPF6：0.5 mol L⁻¹；溶剂：diglyme (G2), DOL；溶剂比例（体积）：diglyme (G2)=0.75, DOL=0.25。

This endows the G2-based electrolyte high ionic conductivity, but regretfully, impedes $Na^{+}$ desolvation. Explicitly, ${}^{1}H$ and ${}^{17}O$ nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) were studied in Figure 2b; Figure S1 (Supporting Information). ${}^{1}H$ (G2) displays an upfield chemical shift in G2/DOL than G2, while the chemical shift of the ${}^{17}O$ (G2) shifts downfield.
